name: 1636 Prairie Avenue — stone-front house, the south half of the pair with 1634, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The south-west corner of the K01 footprint: the draft's rear corner of its main rectangle (lot frame u 22.500, v -1.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line) moved 8.25 m toward the street and 2.75 m south, onto the rear corner of the wide front body (lot frame u 30.750, v -3.750 m), so that the narrow rear part becomes a rear wing behind it. Through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.58 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1636 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1636 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the wide front part of the traced main part s20fp-1636-b1 p3 (data/traces/prairie_1904_footprints_s20.json, T-2328), re-read for the pair by T-2392: 15.383 m deep and 7.685 m along the front. Its south wall is the trace's (v -0.1-0.0 in this frame); its north wall is the party line it shares with 1634, the traced shared edge (median 7.69), where 1634's south wall now stands too; its front is the traced outline's front edge, the outer side of the blue stone band the sheet draws along both fronts (u 15.3-15.4), flush with 1634's. The band is the sheet's colour for the stone front inside the outline: the canted bay stands 0.8 m beyond its outer side. T-2348 had kept the draft's 13.75 m by 7.5 m, the front behind the band and the north wall 0.19 m inside the line. The trace also draws the canted stone bay (p1), built as a K08 canted bay, and the narrow rear part (u -8.2-0, v 2.45-7.65), built as the rear wing in rear_wings.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three full storeys over a basement.

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone) on a brick (pink) house: the register reads 'brick with stone front'.

principal_floor_m.note: The draft rules' principal floor, 1.4 m over the basement, inside the K01 contract's 0.8-1.8 m; 1634's, its partner's.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor, principal storey first: 1634's, so the pair's floors, cornice and parapets run level across the party wall. The wall head stands at 12.3 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as 1612's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house's.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, K02's brown sandstone, smooth-dressed over two rusticated base courses up to the area lights' heads: the same stone as 1634, its partner, because the sheet draws the two fronts as one attached pair in one stone, and 1634's brown is chosen on the Prairie library's text record cgn-1634-text (the Inter Ocean, 10 September 1890: 'the brown stone mansion No. 1634'). Nothing reads 1636's own stone, and that record is not a source here, so the attribute is reconstructed. No corner returns, as 1634's.

street_front_trim.note: K09 cornice-hood lintels on the two lower storeys and K01's flat stone lintel on the low third, 1628's.

wall_head.note: The bracketed street cornice the register's stone-front family carries: K10's timber brackets and bed moulding under the flat roof's cornice box, along the street front alone (the side walls rise into parapets).

roof_form.note: The stone-front family's flat roof behind its cornice, as the draft rules drew it (k01.roof.flat, from K05's k05.roof.flat_parapet, T-2349): a tin deck falling to the rear wall, a coped parapet on each side wall and a blocking course over the front. No source reads this roof.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall to the rear fascia, 2 degrees: the K05 variant's own, inside its declared 1-5 degree band.

eave_overhang_m.note: The street cornice box projects 0.6 m from the stone, the brackets' reach with room to the fascia, as 1628's eave.

entrance_bay.note: The door at the north end of the front, beside the party wall. The draft rules' row mirrored the pair's doors to their outer ends (1636's to the south), but the sheet stands 1636's canted stone bay across the south half of its front (0.0-3.8 m from the south corner), so the door goes in the north half the bay leaves. 1634's bay stands at its north end (T-2392, read off the raster), so the pair mirrors: doors together at the party line, bays at the outer ends.

front_bays.note: Two bays across the 7.685 m front, south to north: the canted bay's on the south (its windows are the bay's own), and on the north the door with a window a storey over it, 1.85 m from the party line as 1634's is from its side of it.

bays.note: The sheet's canted stone bay (s20fp-1636-b1 p1, read in this frame: 3.76 m at the front, its faces cut back at about 45 degrees to a front 1.8 m wide, 0.8 m out from the traced front, centred 1.82 m from the south corner) as K08's canted bay, 3.7 m at the wall, 1.1 m out and a 1.5 m face (the kit's plan, which a record may not resize), three storeys laid in the front's own brownstone (`front_stone`) with a sash in every face, under a low tin hip that stops under the cornice's brackets, its storeys 1634's bay's. Its centre is 0.38 m north of the sheet's, to leave K01's 0.3 m pier at the south corner.

side_bays.note: Three windows a storey along the south wall, west to east, one to each room of a three-room-deep house in the 15.383 m body (T-2392 spread them with the deeper front); the wall faces the side yard of 1638, the Shortall-Gregory cottage.

rear_bays.note: One window a storey in the 2.75 m of the rear wall south of the rear wing, which covers the rest of it (s 0-4.935 m from the north end).

basement_lights.note: Area lights under the principal windows, 0.65 m high so that two rusticated base courses and the coping reach their heads (K02's course range).

roof_covering.note: K04's flat-seam painted tin, the covering of a low-slope deck, with painted tin flashing; no caps, since a flat deck has no hip or ridge.

chimneys.note: Two brick stacks against the north party wall, where a rowhouse's flues rise, over the walls between front, middle and back rooms, 1634's stacks' places mirrored to its own party wall (T-2392 moved both houses' with the deeper body); 0.9 m above the deck's high line. No source reads this house's chimneys.

window_kit.note: Every window from the K06 kit: two-over-two double-hung sash, the kit's commonest form, not a reading of this house; the basement lights the kit's area light.

entrance_kit.note: K07's panelled door at the head of a straight stoop; the front yard is 1634's (its street line 24.61 m from the rear corner of a body whose front stands flush with this one's) less the 15.4 m body (T-2392).

rear_wings.note: T-2348: the narrow rear part the 1911 sheet draws behind the north side of the main body, whose PLACE and storey count are read from the map and whose form is K01's reconstruction. Read on sheet 20 (trace s20fp-1636-b1 p3, the draft's r1 behind the front body's rear line) in this frame: u -8.25 to 0 and v 2.75 to 7.685 (T-2392: its north wall on the pair's party line; the trace's outline reads u -8.2 to 0 and v 2.45-2.7 to 7.45-7.65), its north wall on the party line flush with the main body's. The sheet draws it inside the same brick main part as the front body, lettered '3B' for the whole, so it is three storeys: K01's wing builds from grade to its deck, with floors at the main body's 1.4 m principal floor and lower back-building storeys (3.6, 3.3 and 3.0 m, its deck under the main wall head). K06 sash, two a storey in its south wall and one in its rear, the flat painted-tin deck on a 0.25 m fascia with a 0.15 m overhang, as 1604's and 1616's wings: all reconstructed. The north wall is blank, the party wall continuing.

boundary.note: T-3216: no picture of this front is held, so the boundary is a STATED RECONSTRUCTION on the west side of the block's pictured fronts, every one of which closes its street line and gates its walk: 1612's photograph (an iron spear fence on its curb, a pair of entrance gates at the stoop's foot and a gate across the south passage), 1620's 1874 engraving and 1898 sketch (an iron lattice on its base with gate piers at the walk), 1616's boarded street line in the same 1874 plate, and 1638's photograph (iron bars on a stone base between gate piers). Built as the K11 kit's spear fence on its curb, the plainest of them and the block's photographed iron, with the kit's pair of entrance leaves on stone piers, 1.3 m clear on the stoop's centre, standing open (drawn 70 degrees) as 1612's photograph and both pictures of 1620 show their entrance gates. No side gate: the house stands 0.14 m from its south lot line, less than the kit's gate needs between a pier and the wall (0.9 m clear past a 0.5 m pier), so there is no passage to gate and the iron runs unbroken from the lot line to the entrance (K11's T-3216 rule). The street line is parcel prairie_1636's street corners (data/street_grid/1904.json) carried into this frame, 9.202 m before the front; it is held at 8.910 m, 0.3 m inside the public walk's inner edge (entrance_kit front_yard_m 9.21), as 1616's boards stand inside theirs, because the parcel's line falls on the walk's edge itself. The lot's sides are the same parcel's, s -0.14 and 7.64. RECONSTRUCTED: the fence's kind, height and line, its gates and their set; liberty L-k11-fences-1600-block-3216.

yard.note: T-3216 (the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door, its gates and its boundaries to their pictures; where no picture shows them, a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of 1636's front is held. The walk is laid on the block's pictured fronts (1612's photograph shows a light paved walk from the public walk through its open entrance gateway to the stoop's foot, and 1616's and 1621's walks are built on it): flags from the stoop's foot through the entrance gate, the gate's width, to the inner edge of the public walk; the lawn covers the rest of the front yard inside the iron. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, flags, width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; no service walk is built (no picture shows a side passage's floor); liberty L-k14-walks-1600-block-3216.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D), stone (blue) front, attached to 1634'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-2348 (piece 3 of T-1863) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the main body is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K02 stone street front, K03 brick side and rear walls, K06 sash, K07 door and stoop, K08 canted stone front bay, K10 bracketed street cornice — under the flat roof K01 builds as k01.roof.flat (T-2350), and the sheet's narrow three-storey rear part stands on K01's rear wings (T-2343). What is read: the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 (storeys '3B', brick with a stone front, attached to 1634, the traced plan: a 7.685 m front body (T-2392: on the party line with 1634, its front on the traced outline), the narrower rear part behind its north side, the canted stone bay at the south end of the front) through the T-1840 census. Its north wall is the party wall it shares with 1634 and is built blank. Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k01-1636-stone-front-flat-2348. No photograph, plate or drawing of 1636's front has been found; the Prairie library holds only the Robinson 1886 site-plan crop (cgn-1636-robinson-1886), and the 1638 photograph (a16-cgy-1638-gothic-photo) shows at its right edge only a sliver of dark brick wall. A later reading that finds one replaces the kit's choices here.
